name: Czechia: participant-facing document QC
source: https://trialagents.com/ctis/czechia/en/patient-facing-document-qc-checklist (reviewed 23 September 2026); population items also from the Czechia population guides named in each item
item_format: Each result records the item id, the outcome, a short rationale and evidence (quoted passage and source locator) or an explicit gap.

items.check: The full clinical trial title and EU CT Number are correct in every PIS/ICF version.
Sponsor identity and study purpose are correct.
Treatment arms, randomisation, placebo or comparator information and assignment probabilities match the protocol.
Visit schedules, procedures, sample collection, imaging, questionnaires and participant responsibilities match the protocol.
Treatment duration, follow-up period and any long-term follow-up match the protocol.
Investigational medicinal product route, frequency and relevant handling instructions match the protocol.
Participant-facing device instructions are included when self-use or device use requires them.
No procedures or claims carried over from an older protocol version.
Foreseeable treatment and procedure risks are represented in understandable language; the document translates the protocol rather than reproducing it.
Pregnancy, contraception and breastfeeding restrictions match the protocol.
Prohibited concomitant treatments or lifestyle restrictions that materially affect participants are explained.
Expected benefits are stated cautiously and no benefit is promised.
Alternatives to participation are described where relevant.
Withdrawal procedures and post-withdrawal follow-up match the protocol.
Injury, insurance and reimbursement statements agree with the Part II insurance documents (CZ-O1, CZ-O2, CZ-O-POSTTRIAL) and the compensation information (CZ-P1).
The main trial participation decision is distinct from optional activities.
Optional future research, optional substudies or optional sample retention can be refused without making the main trial consent internally contradictory.
Each optional future-sample choice has the separate signature required by SÚKL or is in a separate signed document.
An optional substudy independent of the main trial has its own information and consent document (KLH-22).
The participant or legally designated representative signs only at the time of consent, not in the blank CTIS submission file.
The person conducting the consent interview signs and dates the executed consent record under the CTR process.
The form states that one dated and signed copy is provided to the participant and one remains at the site.
Re-consent triggers are defined when a child reaches a new age band, reaches adulthood, or an adult participant's capacity changes.

sections.title: Population and document coverage
sections.instruction: Do not rely on one adult PIS/ICF when the population needs different information or consent-givers. Map every inclusion pathway to an information and consent set (requirements.json population_sets) and apply the matching Czechia population guide.

items.check: Every inclusion pathway in the protocol maps to a population, populations are mutually exclusive within each consent stage, and every population has its full document set; the standard Czech PIS/ICF is present for the main population.

Minors (CZ-MINORS): parent or representative document present; separate written Czech information for each enrolled band 12-14 and 15-17; age-appropriate information for children under 12 where meaningful (signature under 11 not mandatory); one-parent signature route; the minor's signature documents willingness and does not replace parental consent; dissent respected and not described as symbolic; re-consent at the next band and at 18.

Limited capacity (CZ-CAPACITY): who gives legally valid consent follows the participant's legal status and the scope of any court ruling; legally designated representative document where required; information adapted to the participant's ability; participant involvement and right to object preserved; no invented representative hierarchy.

Emergency enrolment (CZ-EMERGENCY): the package describes the Article 35 inclusion conditions, how urgency is identified and documented, and how consent to continue is obtained without undue delay; the right to object to use of data already obtained is stated.

Impartial witness (CZ-WITNESS): for a participant who cannot write or cannot read, the witness procedure, the witness's independence from the study team and the witness signature statement are described; witness wording is not confused with representative consent or emergency enrolment.
Healthy volunteers (CZ-HV): absence of therapeutic intent, study procedures, restrictions, risks (not softened for First-in-Human) and the compensation structure are explained accurately.

Pregnancy follow-up (CZ-PREGNANCY): follow-up of a pregnant participant is separated from collection of information about a pregnant partner; the partner's own consent, data scope, record access and follow-up duration match the protocol.
Participant-facing privacy information matches the actual data flow, recipients and transfers.
The PIS/ICF contains SÚKL's required access-to-source-record wording covering monitors, auditors, regulators or medicines agencies, Ethics Committee members and study-team members as applicable.
Sponsor and controller descriptions are consistent across the PIS/ICF and the Part II data-protection documents (CZ-R1).
Data withdrawal language does not promise deletion that the trial's legal and scientific record cannot support.
The separate sponsor-signed SÚKL Template No. 5 is included in the Part II data-protection category (CZ-R1).
For a third-country sponsor, the sponsor itself signs Template No. 5, not an EU representative or CRO.

sections.title: Biological samples and secondary use
sections.applies_when: samples.collected or samples.archive_used or samples.future_use_outside_protocol or data.future_use_outside_protocol

items.check: Protocol-required samples are described with purpose, collection and handling at the right level for participants.
Optional future research is clearly optional.
Future-use wording states storage duration, pseudonymised or anonymised status and the main intended research purpose.
Future-use consent has a separate signature if embedded in the main PIS/ICF, or a separate signed document is used.
SÚKL Template No. 7 is completed for the biological-sample pathway and covers samples collected during the trial as well as future use (CZ-S1).
Withdrawal wording distinguishes identifiable or pseudonymised stored samples from material already fully anonymised or used in completed research.
Every PIS/ICF version contains the EU CT Number.
Every PIS/ICF version contains the full clinical trial title.
Every PIS/ICF version contains the required ethics committee e-mail (eticka.komise@sukl.gov.cz or the specific Ethics Committee's e-mail).
No ethics committee telephone number is given.
Every PIS/ICF version states that results will be available on the EMA clinical trials website (no obsolete national register).
Every PIS/ICF version contains consent for the specified access to source medical records.
Every PIS/ICF version states that the participant receives a dated and signed copy and one copy remains at the site.
The standard Czech submission does not include the English original or a bilingual PIS/ICF.
Each PIS/ICF page carries the correct version, date and trial identification.
Version and date match the machine-readable Part II document list (CZ-DOC-LIST).
Electronic consent uses an electronic signature method accepted by SÚKL (qualified, recognised or guaranteed electronic signature, or dynamic biometric signature).
A sponsor platform's standard e-signature is not assumed acceptable; sponsor-created signatures not meeting SÚKL's criteria are excluded.
Age-specific and capacity-specific forms use consistent versioning and are linked to the correct consent-giver.
Participant materials and recruitment materials use the current content version.
Screenshots are supplied for electronic questionnaires.
The CTIS submission contains blank forms, with no participant, representative, witness or investigator signature.
Witness signature and date fields only where the impartial-witness pathway can apply.
Correct CTIS section and CTIS title per the naming guide and requirements.json.

No drafting instruction remains in the final version ([bracket] notes, 'Pokyn pro zpracovatele', 'Podmíněný text', 'Vyberte a upravte', '...........' gaps, yellow [INSERT/IF/CHOOSE/NOTE] labels); fields completed at the consent visit stay blank.
The document is in Czech (mandatory).
KLH-22 readability guidance applied: clear wording, no unnecessary specialist terms or abbreviations; language review recommended.
Document length and font size suit the population (adults and parents normally at most about 8 pages, 10 in specific cases; larger type where reading ability is reduced).

Minors: 12-14 document simpler and shorter (about four pages at most, no contraception instructions); 15-17 document may approach adult length with contraception information where relevant for sexually active adolescents.
Foreign nationals: no direct translation of an unapproved English master; a certified translation of the approved Czech version is planned as a non-substantial amendment.
Remuneration appears only in Phase I, bioequivalence or pharmacokinetic studies and not for vulnerable participants (KLH-22 recommendation); expense reimbursement is described separately.

The participant-facing package is compared with the Czechia Part II document checklist: correct Czech forms, correct population variants, correct optional-consent logic and a complete national Part II set.
